sample.title: Why Brazil Can’t Hide From Its Debt
sample.description:
As Brazil heads into an election, its debt problems are becoming harder to ignore. Consumers and businesses are struggling with sky-high borrowing costs as the country’s deteriorating fiscal outlook alarms investors. 

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has rolled out measures aimed at easing the pressure on families and businesses while his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, has promised tighter spending controls, albeit with few details. Whoever wins the presidency is likely to face difficult choices over how to bring the country’s debt to heel.

sample.title: How India's Day Retail Traders Lost Billions
sample.description:
Today's financial markets operate at lightning speed, dominated by algorithms and high-frequency trading firms. Nowhere has the impact of this technological advantage been more visible than in India, the world’s largest options trading hub. 

Fueled by mobile apps and so-called finfluencers, millions of everyday investors flooded the market, only to lose billions of dollars while global HFT firms raked in massive profits. Now, as Indian regulators scrutinize the trading of one of those firms, Jane Street, a critical question emerges: should ultra-fast automated trading be seen as an engine for efficient markets, or a game stacked against the average investor?

sample.title: Inside Texas's Growing Political Fight Over Data Centers
sample.description:
Texas has long attracted data centers with its pro-business policies and abundance of land. Today, it’s one of the biggest data center hubs in the country, but residents are starting to push back over issues like transparency, water use and power bills. CNBC traveled to Texas to learn how the growing backlash has made data centers a key issue in the upcoming race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico–and in midterm elections across the country.
